question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered, earliest-owner configuration layers with narrowly defined monotonic policy exceptions as a supported core configuration contract?
rationale: The proposal introduces a new CLI/configuration mode and defines long-lived compatibility and security-authority semantics; tests and runtime proof cannot decide whether core should own that contract.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded V1
options.body: Advance the startup-only immutable model through formal RFC discussion and accept it once the linked implementation matches the approved normative contract.

options.title: Narrow the authority rules
options.body: Require revisions to exact-path ownership, runtime immutability, or the tool-policy exceptions before accepting the RFC.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Decline a core layering contract and continue requiring hosts to materialize one effective OpenClaw configuration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded V1
recommendation.body: Advance the startup-only immutable model through formal RFC discussion and accept it once the linked implementation matches the approved normative contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to current configuration guidance and security-sensitive configuration behavior.
